build.reason: The target recipe delegates to the supplied CMake build, installs libcbor, and links this target against its static library. The changed decoder and callback code has no change-local build guard.

input.reason: The fuzzer passes its byte pointer and length directly to cbor_load, which forwards unconsumed bytes to the decoder; 0xE0 and 0xF8 0x20 are finite valid inputs.

lifecycle.reason: The installed allocator tracks serialization buffers, but the target releases them with free instead of limited_free. Its persistent quota therefore rises after successful invocations until later valid inputs cannot be loaded.

control_flow.reason: The entry calls cbor_load; its decoder invokes the new callback for valid simple values. Success reaches describe, serialize and copy; errors skip those calls, and cbor_load has stack cleanup.

accepted.requirement: Release each cbor_serialize_alloc buffer through the installed allocator's matching free function, so repeated valid inputs retain available allocation quota.
accepted.target_route: A successful cbor_load of 0xE0 enters the success branch, serializes the ctrl item with cbor_serialize_alloc, calls free(buffer), and retains static allocator state for the next fuzz invocation.
accepted.failure_condition: Each successful nonempty serialization increments allocated_mem without the corresponding limited_free decrement. Repeating the valid input eventually makes limited_malloc reject a later load despite the serialization buffers having been freed.
accepted.alternative_paths: The success branch always calls free(buffer) and has no matching limited_free call for that buffer. The error branch avoids serialization but cannot restore the accumulated quota; decref of the items releases different allocations.
